details: CONFIRMED (diff and the worker's own report). The content is correct today: relay queue check is clean, test_refusal would
accept both ids, and the merge guard only re-proves done files the range adds, so nothing breaks at merge. The finding is the
broken rule (an owner decision: HIGH by the judge base; label structured-data: one writer). It also matters for the method:
the next split (test_queue.py at 1342 lines, F1 of a later change) will meet the same need, and a hand edit is what the rule
exists to stop. The brief offered two paths (a lookup by class name, or a rewrite through the one queue writer); the worker
took a third. Size: 30 minutes for a small writer (a `relay queue` subcommand or a lib function used once, both lib copies
synced), 10 for the revert plus a Gap line.
evidence: $ relay queue --help   (no subcommand sets the test of a done item)
reports/split-tests.md: "two recorded ids rewritten by a text edit (no queue command sets a recorded test)"
failing_case: Commit 234f5a4 changes the "test" field of .relay/queue/done/runner-turns-while-waiting.json (line 20) and
tests/test_roles.py::<name> and tests/test_setup.py::<name> by editing the JSON text. rules/structured-data.md: "One writer: a
single library parses, checks and writes the file. Nothing else edits it by hand or by string replacement." The worker's report
says so itself ("rewritten by a text edit (no queue command sets a recorded test)"). Should: the records change only through
relay_queue (its serialize/check), or not at all.
fix_hint: Write the two records through relay_queue: a small function (or `relay queue` subcommand) that parses the done item, sets
"test" after test_refusal accepts the new id at HEAD, and writes relay_queue.serialize; run it once and commit its output.
Alternatively revert both files and make `relay queue show` resolve a moved name; either way keep lib copies identical.
pass_cases: 1. Every change to a .relay/queue/done/*.json file in this range is produced by code in lib/ that parses the item with relay_queue.parse and writes it with relay_queue.serialize (like lib/relay_queue_migrate.py), or the two files are byte-identical to master.

2. If rewritten: the two "test" fields read tests/test_roles.py::test_a_job_longer_than_a_runner_s_turns_runs_in_the_front_s_background and tests/test_setup.py::test_setup_install_failure_todo_names_the_command, and relay_queue.test_refusal(repo, "HEAD", <field>) returns None for both.

3. If reverted: relay queue show <slug> still prints the moved test in a form a person can run (for example a lookup that finds <name> under tests/ when the recorded file is gone), or the brief's "must still resolve" goes to the owner as a Gap.
4. relay queue check stays "every queue item file is well formed".
reason: Both done records byte-identical to master (git diff master empty); tests/test_split_test_files.py:52 asserts the recorded ids are unchanged and the name is under tests/; it fails at f9d5265 (AssertionError on the rewritten test_setup id) and passes at head.
findings.summary: two done queue records were rewritten by a text edit, against the one-writer rule for queue items (structured-data)
